question.problem: Consider a triangle $△ABC$, where an exterior angle at $A$ is ${119}^{∘}$ and an exterior angle at $C$ is ${103}^{∘}.$ What is the measure of the interior angle $B?$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's draw a corresponding picture.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191822/assets/6fc411e7715044257a6818fe63fb3b7bd212c22a2f3d279f282b2b7161be3ecc.png)

   

Let $z$ be the measure of the exterior angle at $B$ pictured above. Since the sum of the exterior angles of a triangle is ${360}^{∘}$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{119}^{∘}+{103}^{∘}+z & ={360}^{∘} \\ {222}^{∘}+z & ={360}^{∘} \\ z & ={138}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can find the value of the missing interior angle at $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠B & ={180}^{∘}-z \\  & ={180}^{∘}-{138}^{∘} \\  & ={42}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $m∠B={42}^{∘}.$
